title: Advancing bodily injury claims through continuous innovation
summary: Continuous innovation is reshaping bodily injury claims. Learn how insurers can improve accuracy, efficiency, and outcomes.
body_markdown:
## Summary


AI-generated demand packages, rising claim severity, and workforce turnover are putting new pressure on bodily injury teams. Static tools and one-time technology investments are no longer enough. Carriers need platforms that continuously evolve, helping adjusters review claims faster, work more consistently, and make better-informed decisions in a changing litigation environment.


A demand package that once took days to compile can now arrive in minutes, complete with deadlines designed to pressure a fast settlement. Most claims leaders have already settled the question of whether AI belongs in the claims process. The harder question is whether the technology they bought can keep up with the work.


## What's changed on the BI desk


Bodily injury (BI) teams are facing three converging pressures:


- **Plaintiff firms have gotten faster.** AI drafting and more sophisticated operations let them push demand packages out earlier and apply pressure sooner.
- **Experienced claims professionals are retiring.** The people replacing them are learning the job remotely, without a senior adjuster two desks away.
- **Severity continues to rise.** Social inflation, medical costs, litigation pressure, and more complex treatment patterns all feed it.


None of that is news to a claims leader. What's new is that adjusters need to find the right information more quickly than ever while applying the same judgment to claim after claim, and the system has to help them do it.


## Why continuous innovation matters


Most carriers already have some AI in their claims environment. The real differentiator is whether that AI keeps improving as claim complexity, documentation tactics, and settlement pressure change.


A tool built for yesterday’s workflow won’t be enough for tomorrow’s claim complexity. Vendor evaluation is shifting from feature checklists to roadmap velocity: what has been delivered recently, how quickly new capabilities reach customers, and whether innovation is embedded where adjusters already work.


## How Liability Navigator innovation supports the BI desk


Liability Navigator brings critical BI insights into a connected workflow so adjusters can spend less time searching and more time evaluating, negotiating, and supporting policyholders.


- **Demand Package Review** summarizes, de-duplicates, and organizes large demand packages in minutes, helping adjusters focus on key medical information, valuation considerations, and injury timelines.[Demand Package Review](https://www.verisk.com/493ff0/siteassets/iso-claims-partners/downloads/verisk-demand-package-review.pdf) handles more than 32 pages per minute.
- **ClaimSearch® matching** surfaces fraud-defense insights directly inside the workflow, reducing system-hopping and creating a clearer audit trail before negotiation or settlement.
- **Provider Scoring** flags billing patterns that may warrant a closer look, giving adjusters another signal for referral, negotiation, or review.
- **Embedded medical-code intelligence** gives adjusters plain-language guidance inside the workflow, helping narrow the experience gap between newer and veteran claim handlers.
- **Evaluation Snapshot** consolidates key claim details, damages, recommended ranges, and actionable next steps into a scannable view, while preserving the underlying assessment model, for adjuster review and decision-making.


## Five questions to ask a claims platform vendor


Look past the feature list and ask:


- What did you ship in the last 90 days?
- How do new capabilities reach existing customers?
- What data trains your AI, and how do you protect it?
- How is the technology embedded in the adjuster’s workflow?
- What is not on your roadmap, and why?


## The confidence advantage


None of this replaces the adjuster. Bodily injury is one of the hardest lines to handle, and it still comes down to a person making a judgment call. Better technology gives that person more time and better information before the call gets made.


As plaintiff tactics evolve, severity rises, and claims experience leaves the industry, carriers cannot afford to adapt slowly. Liability Navigator closes some of that distance by connecting demand review, fraud insights, provider intelligence, medical bill review, and assessment tools in one evolving workflow.


The baseline has moved. Whatever platform a BI team runs on now has to keep improving on its own, because the work won’t stop changing.
